name: Jollof Rice
instructions:
Blend the tomatoes, red bell peppers, scotch bonnet peppers and one onion until smooth. Pour into a pot and boil on medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the liquid reduces by half.
Slice the remaining onion. Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the onion for 2 minutes. Add the tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes, stirring, until it darkens.
Pour in the cooked pepper mix and cook for about 15 minutes until thick and the oil rises to the top.
Add the stock, thyme, curry powder, bay leaves, seasoning cubes and salt. Bring to a boil.
Wash the rice until the water runs clear, add it to the pot and stir once. Cover with foil, then the lid, and cook on low heat for about 30 minutes.
Check that the rice is soft. If it is still hard, add a splash of hot water, cover and cook 5 more minutes. Fluff with a fork and serve with fried plantain or chicken.

name: Egusi Soup
instructions:
Boil the beef with half the onion, one seasoning cube and some salt for about 45 minutes until tender. Keep the stock.
Blend the tomatoes, scotch bonnet peppers and the other half of the onion. Heat the palm oil in a pot and fry the blend for about 10 minutes.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water into a thick paste. Add it to the pot in small lumps and leave it without stirring for 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir gently, then add the beef, 2 cups of the stock, smoked fish, ground crayfish, the second seasoning cube and salt. Cook for 15 minutes.
Add the chopped spinach and cook for 5 more minutes. Serve hot with pounded yam or eba.

name: Moi Moi
instructions:
Soak the beans in water for 10 minutes, then rub them between your hands to remove the skins. Rinse until the skins float away.
Blend the beans with the red bell peppers, scotch bonnet pepper and onion, adding a little warm water at a time, until smooth.
Pour into a bowl and stir in the oil, ground crayfish, seasoning cubes and salt. The batter should be thick like pancake batter.
Pour into oiled ramekins, foil cups or leaves and place a slice of boiled egg in each one.
Steam in a pot with a little water at the bottom for 45 to 60 minutes, until firm in the middle. Serve with pap or custard.

name: Efo Riro
instructions:
Boil the beef with some of the onion, a seasoning cube and salt until tender, about 45 minutes. Keep the stock.
Blend the red bell peppers, scotch bonnet peppers, tomatoes and the rest of the onion. Cook the blend in a pot until the water dries up.
In another pot, heat the palm oil, add the locust beans and fry for 2 minutes. Add the cooked pepper mix and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the beef, smoked fish, ground crayfish, the second seasoning cube, salt and a little stock. Cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach and cook for 3 to 5 minutes. Do not overcook it, so it stays green. Serve with pounded yam, eba or rice.

name: Akara
instructions:
Soak the beans for 10 minutes, then rub them to remove the skins and rinse until the skins float away.
Blend the beans with the onion and scotch bonnet pepper, adding as little water as possible, to a thick, smooth paste.
Add salt and whisk the batter hard with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes until it is light and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a deep pan on medium heat. Scoop spoonfuls of batter into the oil and fry for 3 to 4 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels. Serve hot with pap or bread.

name: Nigerian Fried Rice
instructions:
Season the chicken with a seasoning cube and salt and boil it in the stock for about 20 minutes. Remove the chicken, shred or dice it and keep the stock.
Boil the rice in the stock with the curry powder and thyme until almost soft. Drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the onion for 2 minutes. Add the carrots, green beans and sweetcorn and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes so they stay crunchy.
Add the chicken and rice, mix well and season with the second seasoning cube and salt.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5 to 10 minutes to let the flavours blend. Serve with fried plantain or chicken.

name: Chicken Pepper Soup
instructions:
Wash the chicken and put it in a pot with the onion, grated ginger, garlic, seasoning cubes and salt.
Add the water and bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend the scotch bonnet peppers with a little water and add them to the pot with the pepper soup spice.
Simmer for another 15 to 20 minutes until the chicken is tender and the broth is rich and spicy.
Add the scent leaf or basil in the last 2 minutes. Serve hot as a starter or a light meal.

name: Okra Soup
instructions:
Boil the beef with the onion, a seasoning cube and salt until tender, about 40 minutes. Keep the stock.
Chop the okra finely (or grate it for a more slimy soup).
Blend the scotch bonnet peppers and add them to the pot with the beef, stock, palm oil, smoked fish and prawns. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the okra, ground crayfish, the second seasoning cube and salt. Cook for 5 to 7 minutes only, stirring gently, so the okra stays bright green.
Serve hot with eba, fufu or pounded yam.

name: Dodo (Fried Plantain)
instructions:
Peel the ripe plantains and slice them diagonally into pieces about 1 cm thick.
Sprinkle the slices with salt and toss lightly.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high heat. Fry the slices in batches for 2 to 3 minutes on each side until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with jollof rice, beans or eggs.

name: Yam and Egg Sauce
instructions:
Peel the yam, cut it into pieces and rinse. Boil in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Chop or blend the tomatoes and scotch bonnet pepper. Slice the onion.
Heat the oil in a pan, fry the onion for 2 minutes, then add the tomato mix and cook for about 10 minutes until the water dries and the sauce thickens.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into the sauce and stir gently until just set.
Serve the egg sauce over the hot yam.

name: Suya (Spicy Grilled Beef)
instructions:
Slice the beef very thinly against the grain.
Make the suya spice (yaji) by mixing the ground peanuts, ground ginger, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, paprika, seasoning cube and salt.
Coat the beef with the oil and about three quarters of the spice. Marinate for at least 1 hour.
Thread the beef onto skewers. Grill or broil on high heat for 10 to 15 minutes, turning often, until cooked and slightly charred.
Sprinkle with the remaining spice and serve with sliced onion and tomato.

name: Puff Puff
instructions:
In a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and nutmeg.
Add the warm water gradually, mixing to a thick, smooth batter.
Cover the bowl and leave in a warm place for about 1 hour, until the batter doubles in size.
Heat the oil on medium heat. Scoop small portions of batter with your hand or a spoon into the oil.
Fry for 4 to 5 minutes, turning often, until golden brown all over. Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
